prs.title: Fix infinite reconnection loop in StreamableHTTP client
prs.author: Dharit13
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: When the SSE stream disconnects and reconnection ultimately fails (max attempts exceeded, or the reconnect request itself errors), the transport currently just logs and returns/exits silently, leaving the caller's in-flight request awaiting a response that will never arrive. Both PRs exist to make that failure visible to the caller instead of a silent hang. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: When the SSE stream disconnects and reconnection ultimately fails (max attempts exceeded, or the reconnect request itself errors), the transport currently just logs and returns/exits silently, leaving the caller's in-flight request awaiting a response that will never arrive. Both PRs exist to make that failure visible to the caller instead of a silent hang. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: #2395 is a minimal, contained fix (~15 lines) inside the existing `_handle_reconnection` exhaustion branch: it builds a proper `JSONRPCError` keyed to the original request's id and sends it via `ctx.read_stream_writer`, gated by `isinstance(ctx.session_message.message, JSONRPCRequest)` so notifications are left untouched. This resolves exactly the one in-flight request at the JSON-RPC protocol layer, matching how the rest of the transport already reports results back to ClientSession. #3098 instead adds a `_unwrap_exception` helper to dig a `StreamableHTTPError` out of nested `BaseExceptionGroup`s and raise it — an exception-based approach that tears down the transport/task group rather than resolving just the failed request, so it affects every other in-flight request on the same connection and relies on every call site correctly unwrapping exception groups. #2395's narrower blast radius and direct alignment with JSON-RPC response semantics make it the safer of the two to keep.

prs.title: Fix pre_parse_json corrupting str | None values that look like JSON
prs.author: vientooscuro
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: pre_parse_json in func_metadata.py attempts json.loads() on string parameter values whenever the annotation is not exactly `str`, which corrupts plain strings that happen to look like JSON when the parameter is typed as an Optional/union-with-str (e.g. `str | None`). Both PRs add a helper to pre_parse_json to detect str-containing unions and skip the JSON parse in that case. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: pre_parse_json in func_metadata.py attempts json.loads() on string parameter values whenever the annotation is not exactly `str`, which corrupts plain strings that happen to look like JSON when the parameter is typed as an Optional/union-with-str (e.g. `str | None`). Both PRs add a helper to pre_parse_json to detect str-containing unions and skip the JSON parse in that case. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: #3056 adds _unwrap_annotated() and applies it to union members before comparing, so it correctly recognizes the common `Annotated[str, Field(description=...)] | None` pattern (Field-annotated optional string params) as a str-only union and skips pre-parsing. #2032's _should_pre_parse_json instead checks `arg in _SIMPLE_TYPES` (a frozenset of bare types: str/int/float/bool/NoneType) with no Annotated-unwrapping step, so an Annotated-wrapped str member fails the membership check and is treated as a non-simple type, leaving pre_parse_json still calling json.loads on it - i.e. the same corruption persists for that annotation shape under #2032's approach. #2032 does cover a couple of union shapes #3056 doesn't (e.g. str|int, str|bool), but #3056 fixes the annotation pattern that appears to be the actual trigger for the reported corruption.

clusters.pick_reason: #2395 is a minimal, contained fix (~15 lines) inside the existing `_handle_reconnection` exhaustion branch: it builds a proper `JSONRPCError` keyed to the original request's id and sends it via `ctx.read_stream_writer`, gated by `isinstance(ctx.session_message.message, JSONRPCRequest)` so notifications are left untouched. This resolves exactly the one in-flight request at the JSON-RPC protocol layer, matching how the rest of the transport already reports results back to ClientSession. #3098 instead adds a `_unwrap_exception` helper to dig a `StreamableHTTPError` out of nested `BaseExceptionGroup`s and raise it — an exception-based approach that tears down the transport/task group rather than resolving just the failed request, so it affects every other in-flight request on the same connection and relies on every call site correctly unwrapping exception groups. #2395's narrower blast radius and direct alignment with JSON-RPC response semantics make it the safer of the two to keep.

clusters.pick_reason: #2395 is a minimal, contained fix (~15 lines) inside the existing `_handle_reconnection` exhaustion branch: it builds a proper `JSONRPCError` keyed to the original request's id and sends it via `ctx.read_stream_writer`, gated by `isinstance(ctx.session_message.message, JSONRPCRequest)` so notifications are left untouched.
